references.text: Jacob sends a lavish gift to Esau to appease him before their reunion, a similar strategy to what Israel proposes to the Egyptian ruler.
The Ishmaelite caravan carried balsam (tsori), spices (nekot), and ladanum (lot) to Egypt—the same products that Israel tells his sons to take with them.
'A man's gift makes room for him and brings him before great men'—illustrating the principle behind Israel's strategy of sending gifts to win favor.
Abigail gathers food and gifts to appease David and turn away his wrath, a parallel to Israel's strategy of sending gifts to the Egyptian ruler.
Naaman takes gifts with him when he travels to Israel seeking healing, demonstrating the practice of bringing gifts when seeking favor from a powerful person.
Kings from Tarshish and Sheba bring gifts and tribute, illustrating the biblical practice of giving gifts to show honor and respect toward a mighty ruler.
Narrative connection: Jacob's gift of the land's best products (43:11) meets Joseph's promise to give them the best of Egypt's land (45:18).
Direct narrative link: Joseph's instructions (45:19) directly respond to his father's earlier instructions regarding the journey to Egypt (43:11).
Direct narrative connection: Verse 6 triggers the event that verse 11 attempts to resolve.
Thematic parallel: The father gives valuable gifts as a sign of grace and restoration of relationship with his children.
